articles.title: Delhi AQI Hits 451 as Purifier Costs Put Clean Indoor Air Out of Reach
articles.excerpt: As the capital's air enters the severe zone ahead of Diwali, residents say the machines, filters and systems sold as protection are priced beyond most households — and doctors warn even a purifier is no guarantee.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families visiting Delhi for Diwali face the same severe air; the article gives them the mask, room and AQI steps doctors actually recommend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nine Arrested After Mob Attack on BSF Personnel in Tripura's Ashabari
articles.excerpt: Police said nine people, including three women, were arrested by Tuesday over Monday's attack that injured three BSF personnel, as a search continued for the remaining accused named in the case.
articles.image_caption: Border Security Force personnel in camouflage uniforms stand in a cleared field. Nine people, including three women, were arrested after a mob attacked BSF personnel at Ashabari in Tripura.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora from India's Northeast, the arrests and the investigation into smuggling-linked violence on Tripura's Bangladesh border bear directly on safety in their home districts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Inaugurates Pune Metro Pink Line, Launches Rs 21,800 Crore Expansion
articles.excerpt: The 23-kilometre Pink Line linking Hinjewadi's IT hub with Shivajinagar opens to passengers on November 4, while foundation stones were laid for four Phase-II corridors estimated at Rs 13,500 crore.
articles.image_caption: An elevated metro station and concrete viaduct above a city road. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Pune Metro's Pink Line on November 3 and launched projects worth Rs 21,800 crore.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora with family, work and property ties in Pune, the Hinjewadi-Shivajinagar Metro link directly affects the daily commute of the city's IT workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Bullet Train Revealed: 280 Kmph Test Speed, 557 Passengers, Eight Coaches
articles.excerpt: The BEML-built B28 for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor is rated at 280 kmph in testing and 249 kmph in planned service, with seven standard-class coaches, one executive coach, Wi-Fi infotainment and level boarding.
articles.image_caption: India's first bullet train, the indigenously built B28 trainset for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed corridor. The eight-coach train seats 557 passengers, with a test speed of 280 kmph and a planned operational speed of 249 kmph.

sources.label: Indian Economic Observer (ANI, citing Ministry of Railways)

articles.nri_angle: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor is the route diaspora visitors most often pair with family trips to Gujarat and Maharashtra, making this train the high-speed service many will ride first.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Seafarer Killed as Cargo Vessel Al Jusufi Is Struck off Oman
articles.excerpt: The Indian-flagged MSV Al Jusufi, sailing from Hamriyah to Porbandar with 14 Indian crew, was hit by an unidentified aerial object on November 2. Gandhar Nahim Ajij, 26, of Gujarat died of his injuries; 13 crewmates were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard.
articles.nri_angle: More than 18,000 Indian seafarers currently serve on vessels in West Asian waters, and their families across coastal India and the diaspora follow each attack on commercial shipping for news of their own.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Tourist Killed, Three Injured as Two Helicopters Collide Near Everest
articles.excerpt: A Fishtail Air and an Air Dynasty helicopter collided while landing at Pheriche at 8:11 a.m. on Tuesday. Police named the dead man as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu; an Indian-origin New Zealand resident and both pilots were injured.
articles.image_caption: Mount Everest, seen from Gokyo Ri in Nepal's Khumbu region. Two helicopters collided near Pheriche, below Everest base camp, killing an Indian tourist and injuring three people.
articles.nri_angle: One of the injured is an Indian-origin resident of New Zealand, and the Everest trekking route draws large numbers of Indian and diaspora trekkers each peak season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Navy Rescues All 20 Crew From Hijacked Iranian Vessel After 48-Hour Operation
articles.excerpt: The Iranian fishing vessel Azini, seized by Somali pirates on October 29, was located and intercepted more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, with Indian Air Force support.
articles.nri_angle: The rescue underlines India's standing anti-piracy patrol in the Gulf of Aden, in place since October 2008 to protect sea-borne trade through waters many diaspora shipping and seafaring families depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three BSF Personnel and Several Villagers Injured in Clash at Tripura's Ashabari
articles.excerpt: Villagers allege a local youth was detained and beaten, fracturing his leg, sparking a road blockade that turned violent. The chief minister condemned the assault on BSF personnel and ordered strict action; both sides have filed complaints.
articles.image_caption: A man swings a stick during a confrontation with BSF personnel in front of a force vehicle at Ashabari, Tripura. Three BSF personnel and several villagers were injured in the clash on November 2.
articles.nri_angle: The clash in Sepahijala district, on the Bangladesh border, is under investigation, with complaints filed by both sides and additional forces deployed to the area.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ayodhya's Ram Temple to Be Lit With 1 Lakh Diyas for the 10th Deepotsav
articles.excerpt: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust will light one lakh diyas inside the temple complex with about 1,000 volunteers in five zones, while the city separately targets 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi.
articles.nri_angle: Deepotsav is Ayodhya's flagship Diwali celebration; the city's wider target is 30 lakh diyas across the Saryu ghats, and devotees abroad can follow the November 7 lighting at Ram Ki Paidi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Main diya lighting at Ram Ki Paidi

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall in Andhra Pradesh as Odisha Evacuates 1.6 Lakh People
articles.excerpt: The severe storm began crossing the Andhra coast at 1 a.m. on Tuesday, the second cyclone to hit the region in a week. Odisha plans to move 3.33 lakh people to 1,139 shelters.
articles.nri_angle: Families in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and northern Tamil Nadu face a second storm in a week, with flights cancelled and schools shut; readers with family in coastal districts should check flight status with their airline before travelling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi's Smog Blind Spot: Farm Fires Now Lit After NASA's Satellites Pass Overhead
articles.excerpt: Stubble burning in Punjab has shifted to 4-6 p.m., after India's monitoring satellites pass at midday, so official fire counts miss most large fires and overstate the decline, NASA and iFOREST analyses show.
articles.nri_angle: Delhi's air is the first thing diaspora families check before winter trips home; the real burning trend is worse than official counts suggest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi's Winter Pollution Curbs Begin: Vehicle Ban and 50% Work From Home
articles.excerpt: From November 1 to January 31, non-Delhi vehicles below BS-VI are barred, offices must cap attendance at 50%, dust-generating construction is banned and parking charges have doubled.
articles.nri_angle: Anyone driving into Delhi from Noida, Gurugram or Ghaziabad in a BS-IV or older car registered outside Delhi is barred until January 31 — check your vehicle's standard before a Diwali trip.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Vehicle ban, 50% office attendance and construction curbs begin
Vehicle, attendance and construction measures end

articles.title: PM Modi Says Poverty Fight Is 'Not Just a Slogan' After World Bank Report
articles.excerpt: Citing the World Bank's October 2026 brief — extreme poverty down to 2.6% — Modi contrasted delivery under his government with the 'Garibi Hatao' era, while the brief's own caveats went unmentioned.
articles.image_caption: The World Bank Group headquarters building. The Bank's October 2026 brief put India's extreme poverty at 2.6% in 2023, down from 27.1% in 2011.
articles.nri_angle: The poverty numbers shape how the diaspora reads India's growth story — and how much of it is delivery, how much is measurement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chopper Crash Probe Widens as Operators Threaten to Ground Char Dham Flights
articles.excerpt: Investigators are examining flights before and after the fatal October 30 sortie, a two-pilot rule takes effect November 2, and 11 operators say they may suspend services in protest.
articles.image_caption: Rescue teams carry the remains of a crash victim during the operation in Chamoli district on October 31, 2026. The Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter crashed near Joshimath on October 30 while flying from Badrinath to Dehradun, killing all six people on board.

sources.label: The Hindu via Tech Word News

articles.nri_angle: Char Dham helicopter disruption from November 2 affects diaspora pilgrims travelling in India; anyone booked should confirm flight status with their operator before travelling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: New Regulations for Char Dham Flights

articles.title: Supreme Court Clears Reopening of Tax Probe Against Former CJI's Sons
articles.excerpt: Justices Pardiwala and Chandran dismissed Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal's appeals on October 28, upholding 2015 reassessment notices over Rs 255 crore share sales and a Delhi property purchase.

sources.label: ANP Tax Corp analysis of the judgment

articles.nri_angle: An India tax-law ruling on reassessment limits that matters to NRIs with Indian tax assessments: a post-assessment investigation report can justify reopening, and a 143(1) intimation forms no protective opinion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Delhi High Court dismissed writ petition

articles.title: Anantapur School Attack: Injured Class 10 Girl Stable After Bleeding Controlled
articles.excerpt: Doctors at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru have stabilised the student airlifted after Saturday's saw attack at her Rapthadu school, Education Minister Nara Lokesh said, as 20 counsellors were sent to support her classmates.
articles.image_caption: Counsellors visit a student at home in Anantapur district after the Rapthadu school attack, with the student faces obscured. The state deployed 20 mental health counsellors to support the affected classes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Marches on Ramlila Maidan Demanding Election Chief's Resignation
articles.excerpt: Rahul Gandhi led the 'Chalo Dilli' march from Connaught Place on Sunday, accusing the Election Commission of irregularities in the voter-roll revision, as the BJP called the rally a threat to Delhi's festive trade.
articles.nri_angle: The rally escalates the opposition's campaign over voter-roll revisions ahead of state polls, a fight diaspora voters are watching for what it signals about India's electoral process.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Class 10 Girls Critical After Chainsaw Attack Inside Andhra School
articles.excerpt: A man attacked two students inside a classroom at a government school in Raptadu, Anantapur district, on October 31; police are investigating and officials have not confirmed a motive.
articles.nri_angle: Reports a serious school-safety incident in Andhra Pradesh factually for diaspora readers with family in the state, without unverified suspect or motive claims.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Polio Threat Persists for India Despite Virus-Free Status, Experts Warn
articles.excerpt: With wild poliovirus still endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan, specialists say India's 2014 polio-free certification holds only if vaccination and surveillance do not slip.
articles.nri_angle: Tells diaspora parents travelling to India with children under five why polio doses should not be skipped despite India's polio-free status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Paralysis cases that result in death

articles.title: Ashutosh Dixit Takes Charge as 29th IAF Chief Amid Modernisation Push
articles.excerpt: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit succeeded A.P. Singh on October 31 after serving as Vice Chief, taking over the Indian Air Force during a programme of new aircraft, air defence and indigenous manufacturing.
articles.image_caption: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit in uniform in front of the Indian Air Force flag. Dixit took charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff amid a modernisation push.

sources.label: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence

articles.nri_angle: The leadership change at Air Headquarters signals continuity on Tejas and air-defence modernisation that diaspora readers follow as a marker of India's defence capability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Led modernization projects for Jaguar and MiG-27.

articles.title: India's Extreme Poverty Falls to 2.6% as 496 Million Escape, World Bank Says
articles.excerpt: The World Bank's October 2026 brief credits consumption growth, women's employment and food subsidies for one of the fastest poverty declines in the world — while flagging a 13-to-1 wage gap.
articles.nri_angle: The brief frames India's growth story for diaspora readers: mass poverty reduction alongside persistent low-productivity jobs and wage inequality.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Job Growth vs. Working-Age Population Growth

articles.title: Six Killed as Helicopter Crashes Near Joshimath on Badrinath to Dehradun Flight
articles.excerpt: A Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter carrying five Bengaluru passengers and its pilot crashed into a hillside near Joshimath on Friday; the operator's fleet has been grounded.
articles.nri_angle: Five of the six victims were from Bengaluru, and the Karnataka government is coordinating the return of their remains from Uttarakhand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rafale Marine Lands on INS Vikrant on First Attempt in Carrier Trials
articles.excerpt: The October 29 arrested landing is the first step toward operationalising India's 26-jet, Rs 63,000 crore Rafale Marine purchase on its ski-jump carriers.
articles.nri_angle: The Rafale Marine induction is a major milestone for India's naval power, closely followed by the diaspora as a marker of India's defence capability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: India signed agreement for Rafale Marine jets
Rafale Marine lands on INS Vikrant

articles.title: Assam Minister's ULFA Remarks Spark Row, Sarma Issues Clarification
articles.excerpt: Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said Biswajit Daimary meant the pro-talks ULFA faction that signed the 2023 peace accord, not the banned ULFA-Independent.
articles.image_caption: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: For Assamese diaspora readers, the row clarifies that the 2023 peace accord applies only to the pro-talks faction, while ULFA-I remains banned.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Vows to Serve India's People Until His Last Breath
articles.excerpt: Addressing a public gathering in Banaskantha, Gujarat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked 25 years in public office, credited citizens for his journey, and said he would remain dedicated to serving them until the last moment of his life.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, Modi's pledge in Gujarat — the home state of many Indian Americans — signals continuity at the top of Indian politics from a prime minister marking 25 years in public office.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Helicopters Airdrop Food as Cyclone Arnab Flooding Maroons Thousands in Odisha
articles.excerpt: Four helicopters are dropping food packets at 21 locations in flood-hit Ganjam, where about 43,000 people have been affected, more than 23,000 evacuated and no casualties have been reported so far after Cyclone Arnab dumped 118 percent excess rainfall in three days.
articles.nri_angle: Ganjam is one of Odisha's biggest migrant-sending districts; families abroad are tracking relief for relatives marooned in villages cut off by the Rushikulya river floods.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Madras High Court Seeks Replies on Plea to Probe CJP Spokesperson Saurav Das
articles.excerpt: The Madras High Court on October 30 issued notice — returnable in six weeks — to the Centre, UIDAI, X and Instagram on a PIL seeking an inquiry into journalist Saurav Das's background and a block on his social media accounts. The allegations are unverified and the court has made no finding.
articles.nri_angle: The case turns on citizenship documentation and platform blocking — issues watched closely by India's diaspora, whose own status paperwork is governed by the same authorities named in the plea.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Led Team Finds First Galaxy Whose Black Hole Fired Jets Four Separate Times
articles.excerpt: Astronomers led by IISER Pune's Pavan Vijay Khadekar have identified J023721.13-010528.5 as the first known 'quadruple-double' radio galaxy, with four distinct episodes of jet activity recorded in its radio structures.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of radio galaxy J023721.13-010528.5 shows four pairs of jet hotspots labelled by episode. The IISER Pune-led team found evidence the galaxy's black hole fired its jets in four separate episodes.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-led team at IISER Pune and NCRA-TIFR made the discovery using India's GMRT, underlining the country's growing weight in global astronomy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Traffic Police Announce Vehicle Entry Curbs Under Revised GRAP From November 1
articles.excerpt: Only BS-VI, CNG, electric and exempt vehicles may enter the capital from November 1, with more than 10 lakh NCR vehicles below the standard.
articles.nri_angle: The three-month bar affects NCR families and diaspora households with vehicles registered outside Delhi who drive into the capital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: CAQM invokes Stage I of GRAP as Delhi air quality enters the poor category
Border enforcement drive; three FIRs over fake No Entry Permissions
Revised GRAP vehicle entry restrictions take effect; non-BS-VI outside-Delhi vehicles barred
Bar on non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside Delhi ends

items.label: Vehicles in Noida and Greater Noida

articles.title: Coast Guard Rescues All 20 Crew From Grounded Cargo Ship Off Andhra Coast
articles.excerpt: ICG Ship Sujay and a helicopter airlifted the crew of the MV Sigma Pearl off Antarvedi after Cyclone Arnab, completing the high-risk rescue within 24 hours with zero loss of life at sea.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Coast Guard vessel (file photo). The Coast Guard rescued all 20 crew from the grounded cargo ship MV Sigma Pearl off the Andhra Pradesh coast.
articles.nri_angle: A maritime rescue on India's east coast during a severe cyclone affecting coastal Andhra communities with large diaspora families abroad, and a grounded fuel-carrying vessel now under pollution watch.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: MV Sigma Pearl departed Visakhapatnam at 12.17 a.m.
Cyclone Arnab made landfall along the Andhra coast.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh Offers India's Battle-Tested Counter-Terror Expertise to ASEAN Partners
articles.excerpt: At the ADMM-Plus conclave in Cebu, the defence minister cited Operation Sindoor and offered joint exercises, capacity-building and intelligence sharing to regional partners.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh speaks at a conference table marked INDIA, with Indian officials seated behind him. Singh addressed the ADMM-Plus conclave in Cebu on October 29, offering to share Indias counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners.
articles.nri_angle: India offered its counter-terrorism expertise to ASEAN partners at ADMM-Plus in Cebu, citing Operation Sindoor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Begins Two-Day Gujarat Visit, Launches Projects Worth Rs 14,000 Crore
articles.excerpt: In Banaskantha and Ekta Nagar on October 30-31, Modi will dedicate a bovine breeding centre, release Rs 19,000 crore in PM-KISAN aid, launch metro extensions and lead Ekta Diwas celebrations.
articles.nri_angle: Gujarati diaspora families gain a direct airport metro link, a GIFT City extension and an eight-lane Ahmedabad-Mehsana road affecting hometown travel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Modi begins Gujarat visit and inaugurates projects.
Concludes visit with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.

articles.title: IMD Issues Yellow Alert for Delhi-NCR as Rain, Hailstorms Forecast
articles.excerpt: Light to moderate rain, thunderstorms and winds of 40-50 kmph hit Delhi on Thursday, October 29, with isolated hailstorms likely in Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh till October 30, while the city's AQI stayed poor at 227.
articles.nri_angle: A practical weather and air-quality briefing for diaspora readers with family in Delhi-NCR, covering the two-day storm and hail window and the poor AQI their relatives are breathing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Madras High Court Upholds OCI Cancellation Over Unauthorised Missionary Preaching
articles.excerpt: Justice D. Bharatha Chakravarthy ruled that US citizen John Daniel needed special permission under the March 4, 2021 notification before preaching in India, even without any conversion, and upheld the September 4, 2026 cancellation of his OCI registration.
articles.image_caption: Justice D. Bharatha Chakravarthy of the Madras High Court. The judge upheld the cancellation of a US citizen's OCI registration over missionary activities carried out without special permission.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling tells OCI cardholders in the diaspora exactly which activities in India — preaching, journalism, mountaineering and visits to protected areas — need FRRO or Indian Mission permission first, on pain of losing the card.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Visiting a protected, restricted or prohibited area notified by the Central Government
Apply to: the competent authority, the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer, or the Indian Mission concerned

articles.title: India Invites Pakistan Minister to SCO Forum, First Since Operation Sindoor
articles.excerpt: Aurangzeb Khan Khichi is invited to the November 20-22 Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi — the first senior Pakistani invitation since the May 2025 confrontation.
articles.nri_angle: The first senior Pakistani invitation to India since Operation Sindoor signals the current, multilateral-only channel for India-Pakistan engagement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum opens in New Delhi
Forum continues at Purana Quila, New Delhi

items.event: Rajnath Singh announces the forum in Dushanbe
Operation Sindoor launched after Pahalgam attack

articles.title: India Rejects Patent for Shorter Drug-Resistant TB Treatment BPaL
articles.excerpt: The Patent Office upheld patient-group oppositions against TB Alliance's BPaL application — the six-month, all-oral regimen that replaced 18-24 month courses.
articles.nri_angle: India's free national TB programme is the treatment route most diaspora families rely on for relatives back home; generic BPaL supply affects its cost and reach.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Three Percent DA Hike to 63 Percent From July 2026
articles.excerpt: The hike in Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief benefits 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners, costs Rs 10,016.10 crore a year, and brings arrears from July 1.
articles.image_caption: The Union Council of Ministers in New Delhi (file photo, Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs supporting retired parents in India, the hike raises monthly Dearness Relief to 63% with arrears payable from July 1, 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Upholds Seven-Year Jail Terms in 2020 Riots Death Case
articles.excerpt: Justice Madhu Jain dismissed appeals by five men convicted of culpable homicide, holding they led an armed mob and that failure to identify the fatal blow does not absolve an unlawful assembly.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families tracking the 2020 Delhi riots cases, the ruling shows appeals are still concluding years later and clarifies mob liability under Section 149.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
